```{r setup-mascot_character, include = FALSE, echo = FALSE}
studio_character <- if (exists("studio_character")) studio_character else formals(mascot::mascot)$character
```

### Choose a character for the job

A character helper packages a choice for the `character` argument. Use an id from
the listing below, either on its own or inside the helper. These two calls choose
the same character:

```{r mascot_character-calls, echo = FALSE}
htmltools::tags$pre(htmltools::tags$code(paste0(
  'mascot::mascot("helper", character = "', studio_character, '")\n',
  'mascot::mascot("helper", character = mascot::mascot_character("', studio_character, '"))'
)))
```

### Shipped characters

Use the `id` column when writing a call. The listing also identifies the family
and whether a character is stable or experimental.

```{r mascot_character-listing, echo = FALSE}
if (in_studio()) {
  shiny::uiOutput("characters_table")
} else {
  guide_table(mascot::mascot_characters())
}
```

```{r mascot_character-family-note, echo = FALSE, results = 'asis'}
if (in_studio()) cat("The studio table follows the Family filter in Controls for mascot_characters().\n")
```

### What comes with the character

- Moods: `r guide_fn_link("mascot_moods")` lists the faces and their status text.
- Gestures: `r guide_fn_link("mascot_gestures")` lists the movements you can request.
- Anchors: `r guide_fn_link("mascot_anchors")` lists attachment points on the drawing.
- Palettes: `r guide_fn_link("mascot_palettes")` lists the named colour choices.

Check these listings for the character you choose before reusing code written
for another character.
